title: Plan flexible routes and mechanisms with explicit checks
applicability: Use when the design needs a flexible hose, belt, gear train, linkage or proof of strength. Begin by defining the physical fitting, moving group and property the build must demonstrate.
steps: Start with the rigid mounts and the endpoint directions. Reserve an accessible hose route with enough length and room for bending at both travel limits. Measure bend radius and interference for the selected physical hose during prototype checks.

Mount and retain the shafts before placing gears. Record the input and output axes, tooth profiles, candidate center spacing and expected direction of travel. Isolate open-chain moving groups to sample collisions and connector engagement in BrickLayer.

Check hose elasticity and pullout, belt length and tension, torque transfer, backlash, linkage closure, clutch force, and real loads with tools appropriate to those properties. BrickLayer's rigid placement and motion checks can verify annotated rigid interfaces and sampled poses. Closed loops need a separate kinematic analysis, and real load limits need physical evidence.
expected: A rigid test can report collision, support and whether annotated connectors remain engaged at its sampled poses. Flexible routes, loop closure, force, and power transmission need their own evidence.
